transcript.text: I've just bought an AEG L7FEE865R and the Eco 40-60 wash says 3:39 and seems to take forever. My old machine did a 40 wash in an hour. Is it faulty? Should I send it back?

No — a displayed 3:39 on Eco 40-60 is normally not a fault and, on its own, is not a reason to send it back. Eco programmes commonly take around 3–4 hours because they use less energy by heating more gently and washing for longer. A one-hour 40°C wash on an older machine would have been a different, faster programme. The remaining time can also alter as the machine assesses the load, foam and spin balance. Avoid overloading it and use the detergent dose for your water hardness/load; excess detergent can add rinsing time. Use a standard 40°C programme or a quick programme when you need washing sooner (check the load limit and temperature available on that programme). Eco 40-60 is mainly the efficiency test programme, not the quickest everyday choice. It would be worth investigating only if it never completes, the time repeatedly jumps back up, it becomes stuck at one stage, or an error code appears. Does the Eco programme eventually finish normally?
Yes, it finishes and spins fine, and the clothes come out clean. It just takes the full 3:39 every time on Eco 40-60. Cottons 40 shows about 2 hours, so is that normal too?

Yes. A Cottons 40 time of about two hours is normal too, particularly on a modern efficient machine. It is a different programme from the old one-hour 40°C wash, with lower water use and generally a longer wash/rinse sequence. In your case, both timings fit normal behaviour: Eco 40-60 at 3:39, and Cottons 40 at around two hours. The key reassurance is that the cycles finish, spin properly and leave the clothes clean. There is no indication from that pattern that the machine is faulty or needs returning. For quicker everyday loads, use the machine’s shorter/quick 40°C option where the load size and fabric care label allow it. Keep loads loose rather than tightly packed, and dose detergent accurately; overloading or excess detergent can make any programme take longer through balancing or extra rinsing. Investigate only if a programme starts taking substantially longer than its displayed time, repeatedly adds time, fails to finish, leaves water in the drum, or shows an error code.

candidates: Time adjustment for load, foam or spin balance (medium)
